purpose: Benchmark entry: a real, public, historical DeFi exploit used to measure whether Argus's detection classes catch its on-chain footprint. Adapt the referenced DeFiHackLabs PoC + fork-validate to upgrade SPEC -> CONFIRMED.
mechanism: The AnyswapV4Router function anySwapOutUnderlyingWithPermit() (and sibling ...WithPermit functions) called token.permit(from, router, amount, deadline, v, r, s) before pulling the user's tokens. Two flaws combined: (1) the function never validated that the supplied `token` was a legitimate Multichain anyToken/underlying — an attacker could pass an arbitrary token such as canonical WETH; and (2) WETH (and several other tokens like WBNB/MATIC/AVAX) does NOT implement permit() but has a non-reverting fallback function (WETH's fallback is deposit()). This "phantom function" meant the permit() call silently succeeded as a no-op even with a zero/empty signature (v=0, r=0x, s=0x), so signature verification was effectively bypassed. Because Multichain had instructed users to grant near-infinite ERC20 approvals to the router to save gas, the attacker could call the function with a victim's address as `from` and, with no valid signature, have the router transferFrom the victim's pre-approved WETH to an attacker-controlled address. PoC forks mainnet at block 14037236 and calls anySwapOutUnderlyingWithPermit(victim, attackerToken, msg.sender, amount, deadline, 0, "0x", "0x", 56).

provenance.loss_usd_approx: ~$3M stolen across multiple attackers (~1,889.66 WETH + 833.42 AVAX; ~$1M+ returned by a whitehat; net ~976.86 WETH lost). ~$431M in WETH was at risk from existing infinite approvals before mitigation. Single referenced attack tx drained 308.64 WETH (~$565K).
